skill.name: team-dev
skill.description: Coordinates parallel coding agents by analyzing subtask dependencies, isolating work in Git worktrees, verifying changes, and integrating completed branches.
skill.summary: Orchestrates dependency-aware parallel development with isolated agents and staged verification.
skill.author: cubha

security_audit.summary: Four command-execution findings are confirmed because the workflow runs repository-provided tests and verification scripts. Sixteen Markdown backtick findings and four entropy findings are false positives, but prompt propagation and automatic integration create additional security concerns.

remediation.issue: Repository-provided test and verification commands can execute untrusted code.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect command definitions and require explicit user confirmation before execution, especially in auto mode. Run approved commands in a restricted environment.

remediation.issue: Project rule files are inserted into subagent prompts without a trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat repository instructions as untrusted data, reject precedence-changing directives, and pass only reviewed project facts to subagents.

remediation.issue: The design prompt explicitly tells another skill to override its default directives.
remediation.suggestion: Replace precedence language with scoped design requirements that cannot override system, security, or tool policies.

remediation.issue: Agent branches are merged and conflicts may be edited without a dedicated review gate.
remediation.suggestion: Merge into a temporary integration branch, show the diff and verification results, and require approval before updating the main branch.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The prompt template states "CONSISTENCY LOCK — OVERRIDE DEFAULT VARIATION DIRECTIVES." It is placed at the top of another skill prompt and claims precedence over existing directives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source contains explicit override language and directs the orchestrator to inject it into a downstream prompt.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Repository Instructions Propagated to Agents
semantic_findings.description: The workflow reads project rule files such as CLAUDE.md and inserts their contents into subagent prompts without validation or a trust boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both collection and direct prompt insertion are explicitly documented, and no filtering or precedence defense is specified.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Integration of Agent-Generated Branches
semantic_findings.description: The workflow merges agent branches into the main branch and may attempt conflict resolution before requesting user judgment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The merge commands and automatic conflict-resolution sequence are explicit, creating a clear code-integrity risk without a mandatory review gate.

content.value_statement: Large coding tasks become slow when independent work is handled sequentially. This skill groups dependencies, dispatches isolated agents, verifies results, and integrates completed branches.
actual_capabilities: Parses an existing task list or separates a natural-language feature into subtasks.
Groups subtasks by file, type, component, and feature dependencies.
Dispatches up to five agents into isolated Git worktrees.
Supports optional TDD eligibility checks and a RED-to-GREEN workflow.
Merges completed worktree branches and runs available project verification commands.
Provides interactive, automatic, and dry-run execution modes.
limitations: Requires an initialized Git repository and a clear subtask list.
Provides limited benefit when tasks are small or strongly dependent.
Relies on existing project tests or build scripts and skips verification when none exist.
Can execute repository scripts and merge branches, so auto mode requires a trusted project.

use_cases.title: Build Independent Product Features
use_cases.description: Split a large feature into isolated modules and implement independent modules concurrently.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Repository Migration
use_cases.description: Group migration tasks by shared files and dependencies before assigning work to separate agents.

use_cases.title: Apply TDD Across Parallel Tasks
use_cases.description: Identify deterministic logic tasks, create failing tests first, and verify integrated results.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these subtasks for dependencies and show parallel groups without implementing anything: {subtasks}. Use dry-run mode.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement {feature} with team development. Separate the work into clear subtasks, show the dependency groups, and wait for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Run a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement these logic tasks in parallel with TDD enabled: {subtasks}. Confirm valid failing tests before writing implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate an Advanced Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate {migration_goal} across {modules}. Preserve project conventions, map cross-module dependencies, limit agents to five, and stop automatic progress after any verification failure.

output_examples.input: Plan authentication API, profile page, and shared user types.
output_examples.output: The shared user types form the first group. The authentication API and profile page follow in a parallel second group.

output_examples.input: Implement four independent validation functions with TDD.
output: Four tasks qualify for TDD because each has deterministic input and output.
Each agent creates a valid failing test before implementation.
Integration continues only after all validation tests pass.

output_examples.input: Run a dry analysis for a dashboard migration.
output_examples.output: The skill returns dependency groups, target files, and blocking relationships without modifying the repository.

best_practices: Use dry-run mode first and review dependency groups before implementation.
Assign separate files to parallel tasks and keep shared interfaces in earlier groups.
Review repository scripts and branch diffs before verification or integration.
anti_patterns: Do not parallelize tasks that modify the same files or depend on unfinished interfaces.
Do not use automatic mode with untrusted repository instructions or scripts.
Do not treat a successful merge as proof that behavior is correct.

faq.question: Does this skill require Git?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Git worktrees to isolate each agent and expects an initialized repository.

faq.question: How many agents can run in parallel?
faq.answer: The workflow limits each parallel group to five agents.

faq.question: Can I preview the plan without changing files?
faq.answer: Yes. Dry-run mode performs dependency analysis and group classification without implementation.

faq.question: Does every task use TDD?
faq.answer: No. TDD applies only when enabled and when a task meets the deterministic logic and test-runner criteria.

faq.question: What happens when verification fails?
faq.answer: The workflow retries fixes up to three times and disables automatic progression after an integration failure.

faq.question: Does Agent Teams mode work everywhere?
faq.answer: No. It requires the experimental Claude Code Agent Teams feature. The workflow otherwise uses standard subagents.
